instruction: Search for women's dresses and sort them by highest price.

metadata.explanation: Variation 1: Changed to women's dresses category with price high-to-low sort. Same pattern as original - navigate to category, apply price sorting. Uses similar breadcrumb and URL validation.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts breadcrumb navigation (category path) from HTML class 'pmpSearch_breadcrumb' to verify navigation to women's dresses category
Getter correctly extracts sort selector from HTML class 'sbSelector' to verify 'Price High-Low' filter is applied
Dual verification approach (HTML class elements + URL parameters) provides robust validation - breadcrumb classes and URL keywords both checked
Expected rules structure matches getter output structure: all keys are lowercase (dresses, women, price high-low, is_other_exist) with boolean values
Metric 'check_direct_json_object' performs correct exact boolean comparison between result and expected values
Complete coverage: verifies BOTH requirements - (1) category navigation to women's dresses AND (2) price high-to-low sort filter
is_other_exist flag correctly detects unexpected elements, ensuring only the expected categories/filters are active
Edge case handling is sound: missing keys result in getter not setting the key, metric detects mismatch and returns 0.0, correctly failing incomplete tasks
Case-insensitive matching in getter (converts to lowercase) aligns with expected rules format
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The dual-checking logic (class_multiObject_li + url_include_expected_multichoice) is somewhat complex and could be simplified for maintainability, though functionally correct
Minor: Consider adding explicit logging to track which verification method (class vs URL) succeeded, to aid debugging in case of website structure changes
